messages:
mike: Heads up — saw 3 ECC/Xid spikes on gpu-node-13 (us-west-2) in the last 10m. auto-drain job didn't start; node stayed Ready. anyone else seeing this?

sara: I saw the alert but assumed it was noise. can you paste the raw log?

mike: pasted below from node exporter: ```
[2026-03-17T19:41:12Z] GPU0 ECC=single_error_count=23, XID=31
[2026-03-17T19:42:07Z] GPU0 ECC=single_error_count=25, XID=31
[2026-03-17T19:45:09Z] GPU0 ECC=single_error_count=30, XID=60
kubectl get nodes gpu-node-13 -o wide shows Ready, no taints.```

ashok: Hmm — our signal bridge should be converting those telemetry events into a taint or slurm drain job. looks like the bridge dropped events. i'll check bridge logs. @oncall-bot did we try to cordon this node automatically?

oncall-bot: automated-drain: attempt queued for gpu-node-13 at 2026-03-17T19:46:00Z -> failed (no matching capacity pool for fallback).

claire: ah — the fallback mapping for us-west-2/gtx-4090 is empty after last week's placement change. so the drain job aborted to avoid killing workloads without a target. that should not leave the node Ready though.

sara: proposal: change bridge behaviour to 1) taint node (gpu-health=degraded:NoSchedule) immediately on Xid>threshold, 2) submit a Slurm drain-with-delay job with 10m grace, 3) if fallback pool mapping missing, notify and still soft-cordon so k8s pods can be evicted safely.

mike: agree to soft-cordon-first. our current flow is too all-or-nothing. can we add debounce to avoid reacting to single transient XID=31 bursts? last week we remediated by reset and it recovered.

ashok: debounce implemented in bridge v2 currently (3 events in 5m). looks like node had 3 events but they were split by >5m in last rollout config. i'll update to 3 in 10m and add a soft-cordon step.

claire: cost note — if we start moving pods to fallback dedicated pools frequently, we'll spin up dedicated instances and blow the cost budget. need a cooldown per-model and per-customer. suggest rate limiting: max 2 fallback migrations per pool per hour.

sara: agreed. also add a label on moved pods: redwood.automatic-move=true so billing can trace.

mike: ops runbook update idea: include quick triage checklist and commands. short version below: 
```
# check telemetry
journalctl -u redwood-gpu-telemetry -n 200 | grep -E "XID|ECC"
# soft cordon
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-13 gpu-health=degraded:NoSchedule --overwrite
# slurm (if node in slurm pool)
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-13 State=DRAIN Reason=autodrain:gpu-health
# force drain after grace
kubectl drain gpu-node-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ashok: I'll push a bridge change + feature flag for gradual rollout. plan: feature_flag=signal_bridge_softcordon -> rollout to 10% clusters, watch 48h. if good, bump to 100%.

claire: can we also add an observability metric: bridge_events_dropped_total{region} and an alert when >1% over 1h? this would've caught the silent drop.

asHOK: (typo) ashok: yes i'll add that and a dashboard tile for per-region drop rate and time-to-cordon.

mike: one more edge: nodes placed in private on-prem racks might not have a fallback pool. bridge should skip fallback and only soft-cordon + notify pager. don't auto-evict in those cases.

sara: good call. we need a mapping table: region x gpu-family -> fallback policy {no-fallback|soft-only|hard-evict}. add to config repo.

oncall-bot: quick summary: feature-flagged soft-cordon + debounce change scheduled; bridge metrics + alert added; Claire to draft cost-rate-limit policy; Ashok to update mapping and rollout.

mike: thanks. i'll add to the runbook and put a short note in the eng-infra weekly.

sara: marking this resolved for now. will reopen if bridge drops repeat. :thumbsup:
